messages:
sarah: Hey team — running into a customer escalation where Go requests appear to hang and retries keep firing even after the request context is canceled. Customer on SDK v0.12.3. They hit a 2s per-request deadline but see the call take ~12s and multiple retry attempts.

sarah: Minimal repro snippet they shared:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, bytes.NewReader(payload))
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req) // client is &http.Client{Transport: tr}
// expect: err == context.DeadlineExceeded quickly
```

sarah: Observed logs: first attempt logs "context deadline exceeded" but SDK kicks off attempt 2 and that one blocks for ~10s inside client.Do (no early return on ctx.Done). After ~10s it returns net/http timeout and then attempt 3 starts. Customer sees high latency + extra billing.

mike: hmm. a few things to check quickly: is client.Timeout set on http.Client? that can change semantics. also what does Transport look like (DialContext / ResponseHeaderTimeout / IdleConnTimeout)?

mike: net/http behavior: if a request has a context that is canceled, client.Do should return, but only if the underlying read/connection unblocks. if the server is stuck sending body bytes the read can hang until conn closes unless ResponseHeaderTimeout / Read/Write timeouts are set on the server/transport.

mike: try setting Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout = 3*time.Second and Dialer.Timeout on the DialContext. also set tr.DisableKeepAlives = true in repro to avoid reusing stuck connections.

sarah: customer says they don't control server, so ResponseHeaderTimeout on client side is our best lever. they tried that and saw improvement but still reported SDK retries ignoring ctx when retry loop creates new requests.

anjali: FYI there's a known bug in the Go SDK v0.12.3 where the retry loop used context.Background() for subsequent attempts instead of continuing to use the original request context in some code paths. fixed in v0.13.0. can you confirm the SDK release? if they're on 0.12.3 they'll see retries continue after ctx cancel.

anjali: short patch to make retries respect ctx (conceptual):

```go
// use the original ctx for all attempts
for attempt := 1; attempt <= max; attempt++ {
    if ctx.Err() != nil {
        return nil, ctx.Err()
    }
    req := reqWithBody.Clone(ctx) // ensure WithContext(ctx) is used
    resp, err = httpClient.Do(req)
    if err == nil { break }
}
```

anjali: the real fix in 0.13.0 ensures we pass the ctx through the retry backoff and abort quickly when ctx canceled. recommend upgrade.

sarah: thanks — customer is on a locked dependency but can we recommend a workaround? they can patch their local http.Transport settings. Anything else to mitigate immediately?

mike: short-term: set ResponseHeaderTimeout and DialContext timeouts on the transport, set IdleConnTimeout low, and disable keepalives if you suspect a pooled conn is stuck. also make sure the request uses req = req.WithContext(ctx) before any body-read code.

mike: longer-term: upgrade to 0.13.0 which includes the retry fix + improved retry policy hooks so you can short-circuit on ctx.Done.

anjali: also add a retry predicate that checks ctx.Err() and returns false if canceled. e.g. in SDK config: RetryIf(func(err error) bool { return err != context.Canceled && err != context.DeadlineExceeded && otherChecks })

sarah: I put together a minimal repro program and shared with the customer. will try their environment with ResponseHeaderTimeout set and also test upgrading the SDK.

dev-bot: Support ticket created: #SUP-12345. Escalated to eng-runtime and eng-ml for visibility. Link: https://support.redwood.ai/t/SUP-12345

mike: if you can paste the small repro here (or the trimmed logs) I can run it locally with different transport timeouts.

sarah: posted repro gist: https://gist.github.com/sarah/repro-go-ctx-retry (trimmed). will follow up once customer confirms workaround. :thumbsup:

anjali: thanks — I'll add a short note to the SDK release notes about this customer case so others searching for "ctx cancel retry" find the fix.

sarah: closing loop for now; will update thread when customer tests. thanks all.
